[[File:Leslie Burns InQuest 17 (1996).jpg|thumb|right|260px|Burns at Decipher in 1996. Photo: InQuest.]]
'''Leslie Burns''' was one of Decipher's studio artists on the [[Jedi Knights Trading Card Game]].<ref name="jkartists">[http://www.decipher.com/jediknights/artists/index.html Jedi Knights: Artists], decipher.com (2000). Lists "Decipher's studio artists". Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20001207231800/http://www.decipher.com:80/jediknights/artists/index.html Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="jkrules">[http://www.decipher.com/jediknights/rules/jediknightsrules.txt ''Jedi Knights'' Trading Card Game rulebook (credits)], Decipher (2001). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010820125115/http://www.decipher.com:80/jediknights/rules/jediknightsrules.txt Internet Archive]</ref> In 1996 ''[[InQuest]]'' described her as Decipher's production manager, culling frames from the original 70 mm ''Star Wars'' print for card images, and pictured her at the film editor.<ref name="iq17">Rick Swan, "Star Tours: How a ''Star Wars'' card is made", ''[[InQuest]]'' 17 (September 1996), pp. 54–60; photographs on p. 55. Scan: [https://archive.org/details/inquest-issue-17-images_202008/page/n56/mode/1up Internet Archive].</ref> [[Leesub Sirln]] is an anagram of the name.

The credits page of the [[Premiere Two-Player Introductory Game]] rules booklet (1995) thanks Leslie Burns "for countless hours of pulls, frame by frame".<ref name="2p-credits">[https://www.hasbro.com/common/instruct/Star_Wars_Customizable_Card_Game.PDF Introductory Two-Player Game Rules Booklet], Decipher / Parker Brothers (1995), credits page. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261015192404/https://www.hasbro.com/common/instruct/Star_Wars_Customizable_Card_Game.PDF Internet Archive]</ref>
